case_number: Civil Appeal Nos. 4578−4580 of 2022 (Arising out of S.L.P.(C) Nos.31186−88 of 2016)

parties.respondent: Banaras Hindu University through Registrar & ORS.

summary: The case involved a challenge to the promotion process for Class-III posts at Banaras Hindu University, where the Board of Examiners introduced an interview component not specified in the original eligibility rules. The Single Judge quashed the promotions for violating statutory rules, but the Division Bench set aside that order, applying estoppel and acquiescence due to the appellants' participation without protest. The Supreme Court examined whether statutory rules governing promotion must prevail over principles of estoppel. It emphasized that statutory procedures must be strictly followed and that estoppel cannot override statutory mandates. The Court found the Board acted illegally by altering selection criteria without authority.
legal_provisions_cited: Resolution No.223 dated 2/3rd November, 1980 of Executive Council
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed. The judgment of the Division Bench was set aside, and the ruling of the Single Judge was restored, directing BHU to conduct fresh promotions strictly in accordance with the rules, and the earlier appointments of respondents 3 to 16 were quashed.
